status: research proposal only; no runtime integration, policy registration, or matches
hypothesis: Preserve a feasible multi-turn deployment schedule for a home interceptor when a disclosed Miner has a current route through a corner Flag Bomb screen.
public_contract: enemy occupancy, disclosed ranks and public movement
legal moves and public two-square shuttle history
no enemy concealed rank nibble, true opening, private seed or future event
candidate_gate: Classic only; own corner Flag remains screened by two own Bombs
at least one disclosed enemy Miner has a stationary-other-pieces route to Flag
native selected action is quiet and loses modeled response feasibility
there is a legal quiet alternative retaining response feasibility and avoiding immediate disclosed tactical loss
response_model: For each candidate quiet move, recompute fastest disclosed Miner Flag route tau and capable own guard shortest quiet route d to common diagonal post. Enemy moves next: d+2<=tau permits d guard deployment actions and one intercept before Flag capture. A nonexistent Miner route has no deployment deadline.
persistent_role: Assign the selected capable guard to its post only while needed to preserve the deadline; re-evaluate after every public update. Temporary departures remain permitted when a return schedule exists. This is a prospective role specification, not implemented.
rank_handling: Ranks 0 through 6 can survive ordinary Miner capture; own Miner rank7 can trade to remove the invading Miner. Both count as stopping one invasion, not as equal resource outcomes.
preservation_required_before_runtime: current confirmed own Flag tactical defense, including moved-unknown adjacent threats
native tactical risk priorities and actual legal shuttle
fall back unchanged if no certified useful alternative
unresolved: Snapshot shortest routes do not model future movement of other pieces or hidden threats.
A single diagonal guard cannot cover sequential two-Miner breaches after leaving the post to capture the first.
A quiet defensive diversion may lose a multi-turn offensive Flag race; captures and immediate wins alone do not resolve that tradeoff.
Current geometric alternative predicate protects the moved actor and modeled route, not every other friendly unit.
No runtime cost or playing-strength effect has been measured.
comparison: Existing C10 repairs or retains quiet two-enemy-turn response coverage. This mechanism starts a multi-step deployment before that gate, preserving a response schedule instead of adding a rank or defense bonus.

primary_source.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding
primary_source.relevance: Action correction from a model and temporal safety objective motivates response-feasibility preservation; this incomplete geometric abstraction is not a formal shield or global safety guarantee.
